what_changes: More services move online with new self-service features, so filing and paying should get simpler and faster.
plain_language: TRA is automating core processes toward 100% and adding dozens of new self-service features.

what_changes: TRA is investing in fairer, more transparent and consistent treatment to earn trust and make paying tax easier.
plain_language: Voluntary compliance and taxpayer trust are central goals of KPA 1 and KPA 3.

what_changes: If revenue targets are met, government has much more to spend — total revenue is planned to rise from ~TZS 40tn to ~TZS 75tn.
plain_language: Mainland net revenue is projected to grow from 40,409.6 to 74,843.6 TZS billion by 2030/31.

what_changes: Customs clearance time is targeted to fall from about 4 days to about 2 days, cutting delays and costs.
plain_language: KPA 5 sets a clearance-time output improving from 4 to 2 days over the plan.

what_changes: Expect more digital filing and e-services, but also smarter audits using data and third-party information.
plain_language: KPA 2 expands automation and analytics; KPA 1 strengthens audit and third-party data use.

what_changes: Large taxpayers are expected to contribute a growing share of revenue, with closer, data-driven engagement.
plain_language: A KPI targets large taxpayers’ contribution rising from 30% to 55%.

what_changes: Income tax (PAYE) continues to be deducted by your employer; the plan aims to make the wider system fairer and more efficient.
plain_language: PAYE is collected via employers under domestic revenue.

what_changes: TRA plans to grow staff from 8,775 to 13,428 and invest in training, wellness and ethics programmes.
plain_language: KPA 4 covers workforce growth, capability, health and integrity.
